svg.aria-label: A TLS 1.3 record: a fixed-looking header, the encrypted content with its real type and padding, and a 16-byte tag
svg.text: encrypted: the data, its real type, and padding
What travels, and what Eve sees:
The header is readable, but always says the same thing: “application data, version 1.2”. The real type (handshake,
alert or data) is hidden inside, and padding can hide the true length. The header is still protected: it’s the AEAD’s
“additional data” (Chapter 31), so changing it breaks the tag.
nonce for record n = the 12-byte IV XOR n
Each side counts its records from 0, so every record gets a fresh nonce without sending one, and a record
that’s dropped, repeated or reordered fails to decrypt: TCP delivers them in order, so anything else is an attack.

figure.figcaption: One encrypted TLS record, as the lab receives it from example.org.
